clue.text: Sails South to see how the land lies

definitions.text: to see how the land lies

parts.note: sails are made of canvas, so the material stands for them
S is the compass abbreviation for South

explanation.surface: A sailor heads south under canvas to explore an unknown coastline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to see how the land lies' is meant figuratively: canvassing sounds out opinion before acting.
explanation.definitionFit: To canvass is to survey people's opinions, which is finding out how things stand before committing.

clue.text: Calm down crazy fool of Conservative initially

indicators.note: initially takes just the first letter of Conservative
crazy suggests wild disorder, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A wild Tory fool is told to calm down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crazy' jumbles FOOL and OF together, and 'initially' gives C, which leads.
explanation.definitionFit: To cool off is a phrasal verb meaning to become less angry or excited.

clue.text: Making observations about husband in love

indicators.note: the word for observing goes about, around, the husband letter

parts.note: noting is observing or remarking on things

explanation.surface: Someone keeps remarking about a husband who is in love.
explanation.walkthrough: Love means zero in tennis scores, so it stands for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis love is a score of zero, which is no points at all.

clue.text: Vessel carrying vital stuff from China or Taiwan

indicators.note: the answer is taken from within the letters of these words

explanation.surface: A ship carries vital goods from China or Taiwan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' looks like a ship; it is a blood vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The aorta is the main artery, carrying blood from the heart to the body.

clue.text: No sprinter coming in second depressed trainer

parts.note: low means depressed or down
a coach is a trainer of athletes

explanation.surface: A runner who is no sprinter comes second, and the coach is gloomy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trainer' could be a shoe, but here it is a sports coach.
explanation.definitionFit: A slowcoach is a person who moves or works slowly, the opposite of a fast runner.

clue.text: Regular letters from true cult we trust as source of news

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals means every second letter of the phrase, starting with the second

explanation.surface: A cult member insists the news comes only from trusted sources within the group.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of TRUE CULT WE TRUST spell R, E, U, T, E, R, S.
explanation.definitionFit: Reuters is a long-established international news agency that supplies stories to papers and broadcasters.

clue.text: Prepared to study history or geography, finally

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it at university

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of geography (history ends the same way)

explanation.surface: A student is prepared to study history or geography at last.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading a subject is the British way of saying studying it at university. History and geography both end in Y, so either gives the letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready means set for action, having made all preparations.

clue.text: Not developed outside unit, like most soldiers

indicators.note: the undeveloped word goes outside, around, the unit letter

parts.note: unformed means not yet developed or shaped
I is the Roman numeral one, a unit

explanation.surface: An immature unit of soldiers is still undeveloped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unit' looks military, but it is the number one, I.
explanation.definitionFit: Most soldiers wear standard dress, so they are dressed in uniform.

clue.text: For instance, is taken in by extreme bighead

parts.note: e.g. is the abbreviation for 'for example'

indicators.note: is is taken in, enclosed, by the extreme letters

parts.note: OTT, over the top, means extreme

explanation.surface: An extremely conceited person is taken in by flattery, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: OTT is British slang for 'over the top', excessive.
explanation.definitionFit: An egotist is someone conceited and self-centred, which is what a bighead is.

clue.text: Old-fashioned actor concealing good surprise

indicators.note: the actor hides the good letter inside

parts.note: stager is an old word for an actor, surviving in 'old stager'

explanation.surface: A veteran actor hides a nice surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: To stagger someone is to astonish or amaze them.

clue.text: Performing with small group going around a part of North America

parts.note: an actor who is performing is on stage, so on

indicators.note: the trio goes round the letter, enclosing it

parts.note: a trio is a small group of three

explanation.surface: A little band on tour performs its way around the continent.
explanation.definitionFit: Ontario is a Canadian province, a region of the North American continent.

clue.text: Song one sings about region, mostly hot part of US

indicators.note: the song goes about, around, the shortened region

parts.note: an aria is a solo song in opera

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter of the word for region

parts.note: a zone is a region or area

explanation.surface: A singer performs a song about a sweltering stretch of America.
explanation.definitionFit: Arizona is a southwestern American state famous for its desert heat.

clue.text: Its political leaders are unlikely to get to number ten

definitions.text: Its political leaders are unlikely to get to number ten

parts.words: Its political leaders are unlikely to get to number ten
parts.note: sounds like politicians failing to reach Downing Street, but means a system run by so few rulers that they would not even count up to ten

explanation.walkthrough: Number Ten is 10 Downing Street, the British Prime Minister's residence; the cryptic reading is that its rulers number fewer than ten.
explanation.definitionFit: Oligarchy is government by a small group, so its leaders are few in number.

clue.text: Outstanding victory secured by defensive blunder

indicators.note: the victory is held securely inside the blunder's letters

parts.note: OG is the football abbreviation for own goal, a defender's blunder
a win is a victory

explanation.surface: A football team clings to a win despite a defender's costly mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: In football an own goal (OG) is scored into a team's own net by mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: A debt that is outstanding is still unpaid, so the money is still due.

clue.text: Funky gift hard to pack inside box

indicators.note: the hard letter is packed into the middle of the rearranged gift
funky suggests something offbeat and jumbled, so the letters of gift are rearranged

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Someone struggles to fit an oddly shaped present into a cardboard box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Funky' rearranges GIFT to FIGT, and H goes inside to make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To box is to engage in a boxing match, that is, to fight with fists.

clue.text: The point of entering is to beat senior

parts.note: to thresh is to beat grain, or to beat in general
senior means old

explanation.surface: The entry requirement is to defeat a senior opponent.
explanation.definitionFit: A threshold is the sill of a doorway, the point where you cross into a building.

clue.text: Graduate's university, say, making change about degrees

indicators.note: the word for change goes about, around, the degrees

parts.note: to alter is to make a change
MA is a Master of Arts degree, so two of them give the plural

explanation.surface: A graduate's old university is said to be reforming its degree courses.
explanation.walkthrough: MA MA sits inside ALTER after its first two letters. 'say' marks the university as just one example of the place.
explanation.definitionFit: Alma mater is Latin for nourishing mother, used for the school or college someone attended.

clue.text: Intervened about cold, provided treatment

indicators.note: the word for intervened goes about, around, the cold letter

parts.note: to mediate is to intervene between parties
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone stepped in over a cold and arranged treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: Medicated means given medicine, which is supplying a remedy.

clue.text: Turning-point in special treatment for DTs, we hear

indicators.note: giving the letters a special treatment works them over into a new order

explanation.surface: A recovering drinker reaches a turning point after special treatment for delirium tremens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' looks like a sound-alike signal, but those words are part of the letters to rearrange. DTs is delirium tremens, the shakes of alcohol withdrawal.
explanation.definitionFit: A watershed is a decisive moment of change, from the ridge dividing river systems.

clue.text: People that matter in the Doctor's multinational medical group

parts.note: the Doctor is Doctor Who of the TV series, so his possessive is Who's
WHO is the World Health Organization

explanation.surface: The Doctor's international medical group gathers the important people.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor Who is the time-travelling hero of the long-running BBC series.
explanation.definitionFit: Who's Who is a directory of notable figures, so it means the prominent ones.

clue.text: Dramatic situation in which masked man wields blade

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a ... of action, a setting for dramatic events

definitions.text: in which masked man wields blade
definitions.meaning: second meaning: an operating room, where a masked surgeon uses a scalpel

explanation.walkthrough: The masked man and his blade suggest a highwayman or villain, but he is a surgeon in an operating room.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a scene of drama or conflict and a hospital room for surgery.

clue.text: Take some clothing from Georgia base, going West

indicators.note: in an across entry, going west means reading right to left

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
a bed is a base, as in a bed of gravel

explanation.surface: Someone strips clothing at a military base in Georgia heading west.
explanation.walkthrough: To debag is an old British student prank of pulling someone's trousers off.
explanation.definitionFit: To debag is to remove someone's trousers, so it means stripping off part of their clothes.

clue.text: Bizarre arrangement for heating that's not fixed

indicators.note: an arrangement is a new ordering, so the letters of the word are reordered

explanation.surface: A strange heating arrangement that is not fixed in place.
explanation.definitionFit: A brazier is a portable metal container for burning coal or charcoal to give warmth.

clue.text: What's universally attractive, it appears, in ill-gotten gains

indicators.note: it appears inside the word for gains

parts.note: gravy is slang for easy or illicit money

explanation.surface: Something with universal appeal seems to be found in ill-gotten wealth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'universally attractive' sounds like charm, but it means the attraction across the universe.
explanation.definitionFit: Gravity is the force by which all masses attract one another throughout the cosmos.

clue.text: Warning signs of half the adult population losing head

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter goes

parts.note: women make up about half the adult population
'of' is shown by the possessive 's, as in women's

explanation.surface: Warning signs appear that half the population is losing its leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' turns WOMEN into the possessive WOMEN'S, and 'losing head' drops its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Omens are portents, events taken as signs of what is to come, often bad.

clue.text: Medics outside university with a parent giving theatrical version of events

indicators.note: the medics sit outside, on either side of, the university letter

parts.note: two medics: DOC and DR, both short for doctor
ma is an informal word for mother, a parent

explanation.surface: Doctors at a university and a parent watch a dramatised account of events.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Medics' gives two separate words for doctor, which sit either side of the university letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A docudrama is a dramatised film or show based on real events.

clue.text: Old saw

definitions.meaning: first meaning: old-fashioned, out of date
second meaning: went out with romantically, as in 'saw someone'

explanation.walkthrough: 'Old saw' reads as a proverb; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Dated is both an adjective for outmoded and the past tense of courting someone.

clue.text: Classic violin turning up in slow movements? On the contrary

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means reading the word from the bottom

parts.note: a Strad is a Stradivarius violin

explanation.surface: A fine old violin features in slow musical movements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slow movements' suggests the slow parts of a piece of music; 'On the contrary' flips it to quick movements.
explanation.definitionFit: Darts are sudden quick dashes, the opposite of leisurely motion.

clue.text: As you used to be, in intelligence, lacking

indicators.note: the old pronoun goes in the word for intelligence

parts.note: wit is intelligence or quickness of mind
thou is the old form of you, as in 'thou art'

explanation.surface: Someone is told they were once clever but now fall short.
explanation.walkthrough: Thou is archaic English for 'you', as in 'thou art'.
explanation.definitionFit: Without means not having, so it is a preposition meaning short of something.

clue.text: Victoria and others appearing in shorter miniskirts

indicators.note: the answer appears inside the run of letters across these two words

explanation.surface: Victoria and friends turn up in very short miniskirts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Victoria' looks like a woman's name; it is London Victoria, a major railway terminus.
explanation.definitionFit: Termini are end stations of rail lines, and London Victoria is one example.

clue.text: Old composer died — performed excessively

parts.note: Giuseppe Verdi was an Italian opera composer
D is the abbreviation for died, as in family trees

explanation.surface: An ageing composer dies after overworking on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: To overdo something is to carry it too far, so this is the past tense of going beyond moderation.

clue.text: Ruin of the French city of Paris

parts.note: des is French for 'of the' with a plural noun
in Greek myth Paris was a prince of Troy

explanation.surface: A lament for the ruin of the French capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'city of Paris' suggests the French capital, but this Paris is the Trojan prince whose city was Troy.
explanation.definitionFit: To ruin something is to wreck it completely, a synonym of demolishing it.
